narrative: He is down as Gaunt, close enough to a lady's skirt to smell the orris. The line is given to the air a foot past the ear of the man in the chair. That man sits about three yards from their boots. He does not move. The oak throws the candles back. The rushes are green. The line is done. No head turns at the table to help it. The small figure in the chair is in the same posture as when the floor was cleared. My lord is not in the room.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Died as Gaunt, and gave the line to the air.

entities.name: Sir Robert Cecil
entities.context: Sat three yards off, and did not move.

entities.name: Margaret, Lady Hoby
entities.context: Stayed seated. The orris was in the cloth beside the death.

entities.name: Richard II
entities.context: Shown on stage in A foot past his ear
